dedupe_keys.name: telegeography ip networks research service global internet geography

description: TeleGeography's IP Networks Research Service, long known as Global Internet Geography, is a commercial dataset on the international links that carry internet traffic between countries and cities. It gives used international internet bandwidth and capacity by country and by route, average and peak traffic, the backbone operators and autonomous systems connected on each route, and IP transit prices in major cities, with analysis and forecasts. The service covers bandwidth between 171 countries, with profiles of 79 countries and 129 backbone operators; its 2026 executive summary reports total international internet bandwidth of 2,259 Tbps after 23 per cent growth in 2026, the fastest growth in Africa at 35 per cent a year from 2022 to 2026, and lowest 100 Gigabit Ethernet transit prices of about 0.03 US dollars per Mbps per month in the most competitive cities. A companion GlobalComms Database covers mobile, fixed broadband and voice markets in more than 225 countries and 2,900 service providers. Coverage: worldwide, updated yearly with data as of mid-year. Format and access: online platform, spreadsheets and reports under a one-year paid subscription; free executive summaries and blog figures. Caveats: proprietary estimates built from operator surveys; route-level detail only for subscribers. Simulation uses: cross-border traffic flows and redundancy of international routes for network flow and cascading failure models, and effects of cable cuts on country connectivity. Related records: the TeleGeography submarine cable map shows the physical cables, and PeeringDB and the Euro-IX database list exchange points.
